<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">MarkWest
Energy Partners completed its investment in Starfish on March 31, 2005, and
acquired Javelina on November 1, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">MarkWest
Energy Partners acquired the East Texas system in late July 2004.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">MarkWest
Energy Partners acquired the Foss Lake gathering system in December 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest Energy Partners acquired the Arapaho
processing plant in December 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest Energy Partners acquired the Michigan
crude pipeline in December 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest Energy Partners acquired the Pinnacle
gathering systems in late March 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest Energy Partners acquired the Lubbock
pipeline in September 2003 and the Hobbs lateral pipeline in April 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest
Energy Partners sold most of its exploration and production operations in July
2003 (U.S.) and December 2003 (Canada).</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Represents
sales at the Siloam fractionator facility.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Represents
sales from our wholesale business.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
Partnership acquired the East Texas system in late July&nbsp;2004.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>In
late 2006 the Partnership began the construction and operation of the Woodford
gathering system and compression system in a four-county region in the Arkoma
Basin in eastern Oklahoma.&#160; On December
1, 2006, the Partnership began gathering gas on that system.&#160; The volume reported is the average daily rate
for the month of December.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(5)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
Partnership acquired the Lubbock pipeline (a/k/a the Power-tex lateral
pipeline) in September&nbsp;2003 and the Hobbs lateral pipeline in
April&nbsp;2004. The Lubbock and Hobbs pipelines are the only laterals that the
Partnership owns that produce revenue on a per-unit-of-throughput basis. The
Partnership receives a flat fee from its other lateral pipelines and,
consequently, the throughput data from these lateral pipelines is excluded from
this statistic.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(6)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Includes
throughput from the Kenova, Cobb, and Boldman processing plants.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(7)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
Partnership acquired the Javelina system (Gulf Coast) on November 1, 2005.</p>

<h1 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 41.75pt;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-41.75pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 7.&#160;
Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results
of Operation<a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_131546"></a></font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis
(&#147;MD&amp;A&#148;) contains statements that are forward-looking and should be read in
conjunction with &#147;Selected Consolidated Financial Data&#148; and our consolidated
financial statements and accompanying notes included elsewhere in this
report.&#160; These statements are based on
current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and
uncertainties.&#160; Actual results could
differ materially from those expressed or implied in the forward-looking
statements as a result of a number of factors.</font></i></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest
Hydrocarbon, Inc. is an energy company primarily focused on marketing natural
gas liquids and increasing shareholder value by growing MarkWest Energy
Partners, L.P., its consolidated subsidiary and a publicly-traded master
limited partnership.&#160; The Partnership is
engaged in the gathering, processing and transmission of natural gas; the
transportation, fractionation and storage of natural gas liquids; and the
gathering and transportation of crude oil.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our assets consist primarily of partnership interests
in the Partnership and certain processing agreements in Appalachia.&nbsp; As of
December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company owned a 17% interest in the Partnership.
This ownership consisted of 3,738,992 common units and 1,200,000 subordinated
units, representing a combined 15% limited partner interest in the Partnership,
and an 89.7% ownership interest in MarkWest Energy GP, L.L.C., the general
partner of the Partnership, which in turn owns a 2% general partner interest
and all of the incentive distribution rights in the Partnership.&#160; Since the formation of the Partnership in
2002, it has grown significantly as a result of construction and acquisition of
gathering and transmission pipelines and treating and processing plants.&#160; Since its initial public offering, the
Partnership has completed nine acquisitions for an aggregate purchase price of
$810 million, net of working capital.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
large portion of our cash flows consist of the distributions we receive from
the Partnership on the partnership interests we own. The Partnership is
required by its partnership agreement to distribute available cash from
operating surplus each quarter to pay the minimum quarterly distribution. The
amount of cash the Partnership can distribute on its units depends principally
on the amount of cash generated from its operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Incentive
distribution rights entitle us to receive an increasing percentage of cash
distributed by the Partnership as certain target distribution levels are
reached.&nbsp; Specifically, they entitle us to receive 13% of all cash
distributed in a quarter after each unit has received $0.275 for that quarter;
23% of all cash distributed after each unit has received $0.3125 for that
quarter; and 48% of all cash distributed after each unit has received $0.375
for that quarter.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Distributions
by the Partnership have increased from $0.25&nbsp;per unit for the quarter
ended September 30, 2002 (its first full quarter of operation after its initial
public offering), to $0.50&nbsp;per unit for the quarter ended
December&nbsp;31, 2006.&#160; As a result, our
distributions from the Partnership pursuant to our ownership of common and
subordinated units have increased from $1.2&nbsp;million for the quarter ended
September 30, 2002 to $2.4&nbsp;million for the quarter ended December&nbsp;31,
2006; our distributions pursuant to our 2% general partner interest have
increased from less than $0.1 million to approximately $0.4&nbsp;million; and
our distributions pursuant to our incentive distribution rights have increased
from zero to $3.8&nbsp;million. In total, our total distributions from our
investment in the Partnership have increased from $1.3 million for the quarter
ended September 30, 2002 to $6.6 million for the quarter ended December 31,
2006.&#160; As a result, we have increased our
dividend from $0.02&nbsp;per share for the quarter ended March&nbsp;31, 2004
(our first dividend payout) to $0.30&nbsp;per share for the quarter ended
December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A significant part
of the Partnership&#146;s business strategy includes acquiring additional businesses
that will allow it to increase distributions to its unitholders. The
Partnership regularly considers and enters into discussions regarding potential
acquisitions. These transactions may be effectuated quickly, may occur at any
time and may be significant in size relative to the Partnership&#146;s existing
assets and operations.&#160; The following is
a brief summary of the Partnership&#146;s acquisitions through December 31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership completed the Santa Fe acquisition
closed on December 29, 2006 for consideration of $15.0 million.&#160; Due to the timing of the acquisition, there
is no associated activity reflected in the statement of operations in 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership completed the following two
acquisitions in 2005 which are included in the results of operations from their
dates of acquisition:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Javelina
acquisition closed on November 1, 2005, for consideration of $357.0 million,
plus $41.8 million for net working capital.</p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">31</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Starfish
acquisition closed on March 31, 2005, for consideration of $41.7 million.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership completed the following two
acquisitions in 2004 which are included in the results of operations from their
dates of acquisition:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
East Texas acquisition closed on July 30, 2004, for consideration of $240.7
million.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The Hobbs
acquisition closed April 1, 2004, for consideration of $2.3 million.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to 2004 the Partnership completed four
additional acquisitions which are reflected in the results of operations from
their respective acquisition dates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Results
of Operations</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management evaluates performance on the basis of net
operating margin (a non-GAAP financial measure), which is defined as income
(loss) from operations, excluding facility cost, selling, general and
administrative expense, depreciation, amortization, impairments and accretion
of asset retirement obligations. These charges have been excluded for the
purpose of enhancing the understanding by both management and investors of the
underlying baseline operating performance of our contractual arrangements,
which management uses to evaluate our financial performance for purposes of
planning and forecasting. Net operating margin does not have any standardized
definition and therefore is unlikely to be comparable to similar measures
presented by other reporting companies. Net operating margin results should not
be evaluated in isolation of, or as a substitute for our financial results
prepared in accordance with United States GAAP. Our usage of net operating
margin and the underlying methodology in excluding certain charges is not
necessarily an indication of our expected future results of operations, or that
we will not, in fact, incur such charges in future periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the year ended December 31,
2005</font></i></b></p>

reconciles this non-GAAP financial measure to the most comparable GAAP
financial measure for the years ended December 31, 2006 and 2005 (in
thousands):</font></p>

<p style="line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon Standalone</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue. </font></i>Revenue decreased $2.7
million, or 1%, for the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the
corresponding period in 2005. We realized a $14.5 million decrease in our gas
marketing business due primarily to lower prices and volumes of $0.38/MMBtu
($2.0 million) and 4,200 MMBtu/d ($12.5 million), respectively.&#160; The $19.1 million decrease in revenues in our
wholesale business can be attributed primarily to the expiration of a marketing
arrangement that resulted in lower volumes of 61,000 Gal/d.&#160; This decrease was partially offset by a price
increase of approximately $0.05/Gal.&#160;
These decreases were partially offset by an increase in our frac spread
NGL revenues of $19.8 million, an increase primarily the result of increases in
prices ($0.13/Gal), offset slightly by a decrease in volumes
(1,500/Gal/d).&#160; Additionally, the
revaluation of our long-term shrink obligation&nbsp;increased revenue by $5.8
million in the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to a $5.3 million
decrease in 2005, resulting in an $11.1 million increase for the
period-over-period comparison.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Derivative gain
(loss).</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> Gains from
derivative instruments increased $6.1&nbsp;million during the year ended
December 31, 2006, compared to the corresponding period in 2005.&#160; </font>This increase in gains was primarily due to the mark-to-market
adjustments resulting from our <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">election
not to adopt hedge accounting treatment on our derivative instruments.&#160; The mark-to-market adjustments resulted in a
$4.1 million increase in unrealized gains, which are non-cash items, and a $2.0
million decrease in realized losses, when comparing 2006 to 2005 results.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">33</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Purchased product costs. </font></i>Purchased
product costs decreased $18.8 million, or 7%, for the year ended December 31,
2006, compared to the corresponding period in 2005. The decrease was primarily
due to our natural gas marketing business which reflected a decrease of $14.3
million.&#160; This was primarily due to a
decrease in prices and volumes of $0.41/MMBtu ($2.1 million) and 4,200 MMBtu/d
($12.2 million), respectively.&#160;
Additionally, our wholesale business revenues decreased $18.6 million
which was driven by decreased volumes of nearly 61,000 Gal/d, partially offset
by increased prices of $0.06/Gal.&#160; These
decreases were partially offset by increases in our frac spread purchase product
costs of $8.3 million, resulting primarily from increased prices and an
increase in our unrealized losses on our derivative mark-to-market adjustments
of $5.8 million.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Facility expenses. </font></i>Facility
expenses increased $1.1 million, or 5%, during the year ended December 31, 2006,
compared to the corresponding period of 2005. The primary reason for the
increase was due to higher Siloam storage fees ($0.7 million), higher Kenova,
Boldman and Cobb plant processing fees ($0.8 million), and higher ALPS
transportation fees ($0.2 million).&#160;
These increases were partially offset by reduced inventory losses ($0.6
million).</p>

<p align="left" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selling, general and administrative expenses. </font></i>Selling, general and
administrative expenses increased by $7.1 million, or 60%, during the year
ended December 31, 2006, compared to the corresponding period in 2005. This
increase was primarily due to a $6.1 million non-cash increase to the
participation plan compensation expense as a result of the Partnership&#146;s
increased market value and increased labor and benefit costs of $0.9 million.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income taxes. </font></i>Income tax expense increased
by $6.9 million due to higher pre-tax book income for the year ended December
31, 2006, compared to the corresponding period of 2005.&#160; The 2006 estimated annual effective income
tax rate varies from the statutory rate mostly due to a change in the valuation
allowance associated with the state net operating losses.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue. </font></i>Revenue increased $69.4 million, or 14%, for
the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the corresponding period of 2005,
mostly due to the Partnership&#146;s Javelina acquisition in November 2005, which
contributed $55.1 million.&#160; Additionally,
the start-up of several new gathering system expansions in East Texas resulted
in a $34.1 million increase in revenue.&#160;
These increases were partially offset by a decrease in Other Southwest
of $23.1 million, which is mostly attributable to <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">lower natural gas sales.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Derivative
gain (loss).</font></i> Gains from derivative instruments increased
$7.5&nbsp;million during the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the
corresponding period in 2005.&#160; This increase in gains was primarily due to
the mark-to-market adjustments resulting from our electing not to adopt
hedge accounting treatment on our derivative instruments.&#160; The mark-to-market adjustments resulted in a
$0.6 million decrease in unrealized losses, which are non-cash items, and a
$6.9 million increase in realized gains, when comparing 2006 to 2005 results.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Purchased
product costs. </font></i>Purchased product costs decreased $44.6
million, or 12%, during the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the
corresponding period of 2005. This decrease was primarily due to a $23.6
million decrease in Oklahoma driven by an 18% decrease in purchase prices
($1.28/MMBtu); and a $25.3 million decrease in Other Southwest driven by lower
natural gas sales.&#160; These decreases were
partially offset by a $5.2 increase in Appalachia due to increases in both
prices ($0.10/Gal) and volumes (5,000 Gal/d).</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Facility
expenses. </font></i>Facility expenses increased approximately $12.1
million, or 25%, during the year ended December 31, 2006, compared to the
corresponding period of 2005.&#160; This
increase was primarily due to the Partnership&#146;s November 2005 Javelina
Acquisition, which contributed $9.0 million; a $5.2 million increase related to
the new Carthage gas processing plant in East Texas, which started operations
on January 1, 2006, and a $3.0 million increase in Oklahoma due primarily to
increases in compression and sales.&#160;
These increases were partially offset by a $5.4 million decrease in
Appalachia due to costs incurred to repair the ALPS pipeline in 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Selling, general and administrative
expense.</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160; Selling, general and administrative expenses
increased $22.6&nbsp;million, or 105%, during the year ended December 31, 2006,
relative to the comparable period in 2005. The increase is primarily due to
higher non-cash, equity-based compensation expense of $12.0&nbsp;million,
primarily due to the Partnership&#146;s increased market value; </font>increases in
labor costs of $4.9 million <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">related to increased
costs for our existing employees plus the cost of additional personnel
necessary to support our growth and strategic objectives; higher insurance
expense and taxes of $2.4&nbsp;million; and a one-time charge to terminate the
old headquarters lease of $0.8&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Depreciation.</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160; Depreciation</font> expenses increased $10.5 million, or 54%, during the year ended December
31, 2006, compared to the corresponding quarter of 2005, primarily due to the
Partnership&#146;s November 2005 Javelina Acquisition, which contributed $5.4
million; and $2.9 million in East Texas primarily related to the <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">to the new Carthage gas processing </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">34</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">plant and Blocker gathering system.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Earnings (losses) from
unconsolidated affiliates.</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">
Earnings (losses) from unconsolidated affiliates are primarily related to the
Partnership&#146;s investment in Starfish, a joint venture with Enbridge Offshore
Pipelines LLC.&#160; The Partnership accounts
for its 50% interest using the equity method, and the financial results for
Starfish are included as earnings (losses) from unconsolidated affiliates.
During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Partnership&#146;s earnings from
unconsolidated affiliates increased $7.5 million due to the restoration of
operations resulting from the completion of the majority of repairs necessary
after the 2005 hurricane season.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Interest expense and amortization of
deferred financing costs (a component of interest expense).</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> Interest and amortization expense increased
$20.5&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, relative to
the comparable period in 2005, primarily due to increased debt levels resulting
from the financing of our November 2005 Javelina acquisition and higher
interest rates. The increase in the amortization relative to the comparable
period in 2005 is attributable to deferred financing costs associated with our
debt refinancing completed in 2006. Deferred financing costs are being
amortized over the terms of the related obligations, which approximate the
effective interest method.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Miscellaneous income.</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160;
Miscellaneous income increased by $11.0 million during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2006, relative to the comparable period in 2005, due almost
entirely to the Partnership recognizing $11.0 million of income from insurance
claims, net of Starfish insurance premiums, recovered as a result from damages
from Hurricane Rita.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Texas Margin tax.</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160; The State
of Texas passed a new tax law that subjects the Partnership to an entity-level
tax on the portion of its income that is generated in Texas. We recorded a
deferred tax liability of $0.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2006,
related to the Partnership&#146;s temporary differences that are expected to reverse
in future periods.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Year ended December 31, 2005, compared to the year ended December 31,
2004</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon Standalone</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenues.</font></i> Revenues increased
$59.3 million, or 27%, for the year ended December 31, 2005, compared to the
corresponding period of 2004.&#160; Higher
volumes and better pricing drove revenue in our wholesale propane marketing
business, representing a $30.9 million increase in revenue, and our gas
marketing business, representing an $18.8 million increase.&#160; NGL product revenues increased $18.5 million
due to favorable pricing, offset by a decrease in volumes.&#160; Increases to revenues were offset by a $5.2
million unfavorable mark-to-market adjustment to replacement gas that resulted
from an increase in natural gas prices, and a $1.0 million decrease in Michigan
operations, primarily from a reduction in volumes.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Derivative gain
(loss).</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> Losses from
derivative instruments decreased $2.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December
31, 2005, compared to the corresponding period in 2004.&#160; </font>This decrease in losses was primarily due to the mark-to-market
adjustments resulting from our <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">election
not to adopt hedge accounting treatment on our derivative instruments.&#160; The mark-to-market adjustments resulted in a
$0.1million decrease in unrealized losses, which are non-cash items, and a $2.3
million decrease in realized losses, when comparing 2005 to 2004 results.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Purchased product costs.</font></i>&#160; Purchased product costs increased $72.2
million, or 39%, for the year ended December 31, 2005, compared to the
corresponding period of 2004.&#160; The
increase was primarily due to volumes from our wholesale propane marketing
business, a $30.7 million increase and our gas marketing business, an $18.1
million increase.&#160; NGL </p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">product

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Facility expenses.</font></i>&#160; Facility expenses decreased by approximately
$3.4 million, or 14%, during the year ended December 31, 2005, compared to

decrease was the result of a $1.4 million favorable fuel reimbursement at our
Kenova, Cobb and Boldman facilities, a reduction to inventory losses at the

<p align="left" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selling, general and administrative expenses.&#160; </font></i>Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased by
$0.2 million, or 2%, during the year ended December 31, 2005, compared to the
corresponding period of 2004 as a result of a decrease in compensation expense
attributed to the Participation Plan and the 1996 Stock Incentive Plan and 1996
Non-employee Director Stock Option Plan, and an increase to allocations of
selling, general and administrative expenses to the Partnership.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income taxes. </font></i>Income tax benefit increased
by $1.9 million due to lower pre-tax book income for the year ended December
31, 2005, compared to the corresponding period of 2004. The 2005 estimated
annual effective income tax rate varies from the statutory rate mostly due to a
change in the valuation allowance associated with state net operating losses.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenues.&#160; </font></i>Revenues for the year ended December 31, 2005, were higher by $198.8
million, or 66%, compared to 2004.&#160; The
increase was primarily due to higher volumes and natural gas prices in the
Partnership&#146;s Oklahoma operations, $80.3 million, and Other Southwest
operations, $37.2 million, as well as operating the East Texas system for a
full year, $64.3 million.&#160; Revenues reflected nine months of activity
during 2005 compared to two months of activity during 2004.&#160; Revenue also increased in Oklahoma during the
year ended December 31, 2005 relative to the corresponding period of 2004 due
to increased well volumes contracted to the gathering system, higher crude oil
prices enhancing condensate sales and higher liquids revenue that resulted from
ethane recovery during 2005 versus ethane rejection during 2004 that
contributed to incremental revenue of $42.0 million. In addition, Other
Southwest revenues increased $21.3 million due to a 27% increase in natural gas
volumes, primarily on the Appleby and Edwards gathering systems.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Derivative gain
(loss).</font></i><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> Losses from
derivative instruments increased $1.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December
31, 2005, compared to the corresponding period in 2004.&#160; </font>This increase in losses was primarily due to the mark-to-market
adjustments resulting from our <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">electing
not to adopt hedge accounting treatment on our derivative instruments.&#160; The mark-to-market adjustments resulted in a
$0.6 million increase in unrealized losses, which are non-cash items, and a
$0.4 million increase in realized losses, when comparing 2005 to 2004 results.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Purchased
product costs.</font></i>&#160; Purchased product costs were higher during
the year ended December 31, 2005, by $155.3 million, or 73%, compared to
2004.&#160; The combination of an increase in purchased volumes and price contributed to
increases in Oklahoma and Other Southwest, primarily Appleby and Edwards, of
$75.5 million and $37.1 million, respectively.&#160;
In addition, the Partnership&#146;s July 30, 2004, East Texas system
acquisition had incremental purchased product costs of $35.3 million due, in
part, to being operational for a full year, but also higher prices.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Facility

$18.1 million, or 60%, during the year ended December 31, 2005, relative to
2004.&#160; East Texas accounted for $7.2

well as performing repairs and a global overhaul of our compressors.&#160; Appalachia increased $5.9 million due, in
part, to repairs to the ALPS pipeline.&#160;
Gulf Coast, acquired November 1, 2005, contributed $2.2 million to the
increase.&#160; Oklahoma, $1.3 million, and
Other Southwest, $1.3 million, increased due to repairs and an overhaul of
compressors.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selling, general and administrative expenses.&#160; </font></i>Selling, general and
administrative expenses, which are not allocated to segments by the
Partnership, increased by $5.4 million, or 34%, during the year ended December
31, 2005, compared to 2004 as a result of the increase in incentive
compensation expense of $1.9 million, and audit and external Sarbanes-Oxley
related costs of $2.1 million.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Depreciation.&#160; </font></i>Depreciation expense
increased $4.0 million, or 26%, during the year ended December 31, 2005,
compared to 2004 primarily due to the Partnership&#146;s 2004 East Texas
acquisition, $3.3 million, and 2005 Gulf Coast acquisition, $1.1 million.&#160; These changes were offset by a decrease in
depreciation in Appalachia, due to accelerated depreciation in 2004 for the old
Cobb facility.</p>

<h1 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and
Estimates</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our discussion and
analysis of financial condition and results of operations are based on our
consolidated financial statements, prepared in accordance with accounting
principles generally accepted in the United States of America and contained
within this report.&#160; The preparation of
these statements requires us to make certain assumptions and estimates that
affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses as
well as the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of our
financial statements. We base our assumptions and estimates on historical
experience and other sources that we believe to be reasonable at the time.
Actual results may vary from our estimates due to changes in circumstances,
weather, politics, global economics, mechanical problems, general business
conditions and other factors. Our significant accounting policies are detailed
in Note 2 to our consolidated financial statements. We have outlined below
certain of these policies as being of particular importance to the portrayal of
our financial position and results of operations and which require the
application of significant judgment by our management.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company generates the majority of its revenues
from natural gas gathering and processing, NGL fractionation, transportation
and storage, and crude oil gathering and transportation. While all of these
services constitute midstream energy operations, the Partnership provides its
services pursuant to six different types of arrangements.&#160; In many cases, the Partnership provides
services under contracts that contain a combination of more than one of the
arrangements.&#160; <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The terms of the Partnership&#146;s contracts vary based on gas quality
conditions, the competitive environment when the contracts are signed and
customer requirements.</font>&#160; Under all
of the arrangements, revenue is recognized at the time the product is delivered
and title is transferred. It is upon delivery and title transfer that the
Partnership meets all four revenue recognition criteria, and it is at such time
that the Partnership recognizes revenue.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue and
Expense Accruals</font></i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">We routinely make accruals based on estimates for both
revenues and expenses due to the timing of compiling billing information,
receiving certain third party information and reconciling our records with
those of third parties.&nbsp; The delayed information from third parties
includes, among other things, actual volumes purchased, transported or sold,
adjustments to inventory and invoices for purchases, actual natural gas and NGL
deliveries and other operating expenses.&nbsp; We make accruals to reflect
estimates for these items based on our internal records and information from
third parties.&nbsp; Most of the estimated accruals are reversed in the
following month when actual information is received from third parties and our
internal records have been reconciled.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Derivative Instruments</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;line-height:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Statement of Financial
Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;)<i>  </i>No.&nbsp;133,
<i>Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging
Activities, (</i>&#147;SFAS 133&#148;) established accounting and reporting
standards requiring that derivative instruments (including certain derivative
instruments embedded in other contracts) be recorded at fair value and included
in the consolidated balance sheet as assets or liabilities.&#160; The accounting for changes in the fair value
of a derivative instrument depends on the intended use of the derivative and
the resulting designation, which is established at the inception.&#160; To the extent derivative instruments designated
as cash flow hedges are effective, changes in fair value are recognized in
other comprehensive income until the underlying hedged item is recognized in
earnings.&#160; Effectiveness is </font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;">evaluated by the derivative instrument&#146;s ability to
offset changes in fair value or cash flows of the underlying hedged item.&#160; Any change in the fair value resulting from
ineffectiveness is recognized immediately in earnings.&#160; Changes in the fair value of derivative
instruments designated as fair value hedges, as well as the changes in the fair
value of the underlying hedged item, are recognized currently in earnings.&#160; Any differences between the </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">38</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='38',FILE='C:\fc\6615415754_D10496_1825455\5860-1-bh.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Mar  7 15:42 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">changes in the fair
values of the hedged item and the derivative instrument represent gains or
losses from ineffectiveness.&#160; To the
extent that the Company elects hedge accounting treatment for specific
derivatives, the Company formally documents, designates and assesses the
effectiveness.&#160; As of December 31, 2006
and 2005, no transactions had been designated for hedge accounting treatment.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In the course of
normal operations, the Company routinely enters into contracts such as forward
physical contracts for the purchase and sale of natural gas, propane, and other
NGLs, that under SFAS 133, qualify for and are designated as a <a name="HH_1">normal</a>  <a name="HH_2">purchase</a> and sales contracts. In
general, the Company exempts these types of contracts from the mark-to-market
requirements of SFAS 133 and instead accounts for them using accrual
accounting.</font></p>

are not designated as normal  <a name="HH_4">purchase</a> and

component of revenue or purchase product costs.&#160;

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company
accounts for income taxes under the asset and liability method pursuant to the
SFAS No. 109, <i>Accounting for Income Taxes</i> (&#147;SFAS 109&#148;). Under SFAS 109,
deferred income taxes are recognized for the future tax consequences
attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of
existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax basis and net operating
loss and credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured
using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in
which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The
effect of any tax rate change on deferred taxes is recognized in the period
that includes the enactment date of the tax rate change. Realizability of
deferred tax assets is assessed and, if not more likely than not, a valuation
allowance is recorded to write down the deferred tax assets to their net
realizable value.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Intangible Assets</font></i></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s intangible assets are comprised of customer contracts and
relationships acquired in business combinations, recorded under the purchase
method of accounting at their estimated fair values at the date of
acquisition.&#160; Using relevant information
and assumptions, management determines the fair value of acquired identifiable
intangible assets.&#160; Fair value is
generally calculated as the present value of estimated future cash flows using
a risk-adjusted discount rate.&#160; The key
assumptions include contract renewals, economic incentives to retain customers,
historical volumes, current and future capacity of the gathering system,
pricing volatility, and the discount rate.&#160;
Amortization of intangibles with definite lives is calculated using the
straight-line method over the estimated useful life of the intangible
asset.&#160; The estimated economic life is
determined by assessing the life of the assets to which the contracts or
relationships relate, the likelihood of renewals, competitive factors,
regulatory or legal provisions, and maintenance and renewal costs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company evaluates its long-lived assets, including
intangibles, for impairment when events or changes in circumstances warrant
such a review.&#160; A long-lived asset group
is considered impaired when the estimated undiscounted cash flows from such
asset group are less than the asset group&#146;s carrying value.&#160; In that event, a loss is recognized to the
extent that the carrying value exceeds the fair value of the long-lived asset
group.&#160; Fair value is determined
primarily using estimated discounted cash flows.&#160; Management considers the volume of reserves
behind the asset and future NGL product and natural gas prices to estimate cash
flows. The amount of additional reserves developed by future drilling activity
depends, in part, on expected natural gas prices.&#160; Projections of reserves, drilling activity
and future commodity prices are inherently subjective and contingent upon a
number of variable factors, many of which are difficult to forecast.&#160; Any significant variance in any of these
assumptions or factors could materially affect future cash flows, which could
result in the impairment of an asset.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For assets identified
to be disposed of in the future, the carrying value of these assets is compared
to the estimated fair value, less the cost to sell, to determine if impairment
is required. Until the assets are disposed of, an estimate of the fair value is
re-determined when related events or circumstances change.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock and
Incentive Compensation Plans</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company adopted the SFAS No. 123R, <i>Accounting
for Stock-Based Compensation</i>
(&#147;SFAS 123R&#148;) on January 1, 2006, using the modified prospective method.
Prior to adopting SFAS 123R, the Company elected to measure compensation
expense for equity-based employee compensation plans as prescribed by
Accounting Principles Board Opinion No. 25 (&#147;APB 25&#148;), <i>Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees</i>.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
SFAS 123R, compensation expense is based on the fair value of the award.&#160; SFAS 123R classifies </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">39</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">stock-based compensation
as either equity or liability awards. The fair value on the date of grant for
an award classified as equity is recognized over the requisite service period,
with a corresponding credit to equity (generally, paid-in capital). The
requisite service period is the period during which an individual is required
to provide a service in exchange for the award. The requisite service period is
estimated based on an analysis of the terms of the share-based payment award.
Compensation expense for a liability award is based on the award&#146;s fair value,
remeasured at each reporting date until the date of settlement. Additionally,
compensation expense is reduced for an estimate of expected award forfeitures.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock Options</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Historically,
stock options were issued under the Company&#146;s 1996 Stock Incentive Plan and
1996 Non-employee Director Stock Option Plan, (together the &#147;1996 Plans&#148;).&#160; In June 2006 shareholders approved the 2006
Stock Incentive Plan (the &#147;2006 Plan&#148;) to replace the 1996 Plans.&#160; Under SFAS 123R, our stock options are
categorized as equity awards.&nbsp; Compensation expense for stock options is
measured based on the grant date fair value and is amortized into earnings over
the service period as the options vest.&#160;
While it was determined in 2005 that the Company does not intend to
issue stock options in the future, they are available for issuance under the
2006 Plan.&#160;&#160; On December 1, 2006 a board
resolution provided for the accelerated vesting of 14,950 unvested stock option
grants.&#160; Consequently, as of December 31,
2006 the Company had no remaining unvested options or any unrecognized
compensation expense pertaining to options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Stock</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company issued restricted stock under the 1996 Plans until the adoption of the
2006 Plan at which point all new shares are, and will be, issued pursuant to
the rules of the 2006 Plan.&#160; Under SFAS
123R, our restricted stock qualifies as an equity award. Accordingly, it is
measured at the grant date fair value and the associated compensation expense
is recognized over the requisite service period.&#160; The restricted stock vests equally over a
three year period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Participation
Plan</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company has also entered into arrangements with certain directors and employees
of the Company referred to as the Participation Plan.&nbsp; Under this plan,
the Company sells subordinated units of the Partnership or interests in the
Partnership&#146;s general partner, under a purchase and sale agreement.&nbsp; Both
the subordinated unit and general partner interest transactions are considered
compensatory arrangements due to the put-and-call provisions and the associated
valuation being based on a formula instead of an independent third party valuation.&#160; The subordinated units convert to common
units after a holding period. Historically, the Company has settled the
subordinated units for cash when individuals leave the Company.&#160; The general partner interests have no
definite term, but historically have been settled for cash when the employee
leaves the Company. Under SFAS 123R, the subordinated units and general partner
interests are classified as liability awards.&#160;
As a result, the Company is required to mark to market the subordinated
unit and general partner interest valuations at the end of each period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
Topic 1-B of the codification of the Staff Accounting Bulletins, Allocation of
Expenses and Related Disclosure in Financial Statements of Subsidiaries,
Divisions or Lesser Business Components of Another Entity, some portion of
compensation expense related to services provided by MarkWest Hydrocarbon&#146;s
employees and directors recognized under the Participation Plan should be
allocated to the Partnership.&nbsp; The allocation is based on the percent of time
each employee devotes to the Company.&nbsp; Compensation attributable to
interests sold to individuals who serve on both the board of MarkWest
Hydrocarbon and the Board of Directors of the Partnership&#146;s general partner is
allocated equally.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Units</font></i></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership issues restricted units under the
MarkWest Energy Partners, L.P. Long-Term Incentive Plan.&#160; A restricted unit is a &#147;phantom&#148; unit that
entitles the grantee to receive a common unit upon the vesting of the phantom unit
or, at the discretion of the Compensation Committee, cash equivalent to the
value of a common unit.&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">The
restricted units are treated as liability awards under SFAS 123R.&#160; As a
result, the Partnership is required to mark to market the awards at the end of
each reporting period.&#160; Compensation
expense is remeasured for the phantom unit grants using the market price of
MarkWest Energy Partners&#146; common units at each reporting date. The fair value
of the units awarded is amortized into earnings over the period of service and
is adjusted monthly for the change in the fair value of the unvested units
granted.&#160; The phantom units vest equally
over a three year period.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">40</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Vesting

The general partner of the Partnership may also elect to accelerate the

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon Standalone</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
primary source of liquidity to meet operating expenses and fund capital
expenditures is cash flow from operations, principally from the marketing of
NGL and quarterly distributions received from MarkWest Energy Partners.&nbsp;
We believe that cash flow from operations and distributions from the
Partnership will be sufficient to fund capital expenditures and other working
capital expenditures for the foreseeable future.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
October 13, 2006, the Company completed the repurchase&nbsp;of a 0.5% interest
in the general partner.&#160; This purchase
resulted in an increase in our ownership level in the general partner to
89.7%.&#160; As of December 31, 2006, we still
owned 89.7% of the general partner of MarkWest Energy Partners, excluding
interests held by certain employees and directors but deemed owned by the
Company through the Participation Plan.&#160;
The general partner of MarkWest Energy Partners owns the 2% general
partner interest and all of the incentive distribution rights.&nbsp; The
incentive distribution rights entitle us to receive an increasing percentage of
cash distributed by the Partnership as certain target distribution levels are
reached.&nbsp; Specifically, they entitle us to receive 13% of all cash
distributed in a quarter after each unit has received $0.275 for that quarter;
23% of all cash distributed after each unit has received $0.3125 for that quarter;
and 48% of all cash distributed after each unit has received $0.375 for that
quarter.&nbsp; For the year ended December 31, 2006, we received $8.8 million
in distributions from our limited units and $11.3 million from our general
partner interest, of which $10.1 million represented payments on incentive
distribution rights.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash
flows generated from our NGL marketing and natural gas supply operations are
subject to volatility in energy prices, especially prices for NGLs and natural
gas.&nbsp; Our cash flows are enhanced in periods when NGL prices are high
relative to the price of the natural gas we purchase to satisfy our &#147;keep-whole&#148;
contractual arrangements in Appalachia.&nbsp; Conversely, they are reduced in
periods when the NGL prices are low relative to the price of natural gas we
purchase to satisfy such contractual arrangements.&nbsp; Under &#147;keep-whole&#148;
contracts, we retain and sell the NGLs produced in our processing operations
for third-party producers, and then reimburse or &#147;keep-whole&#148; the producers for
the energy content of the NGLs removed through the re-delivery to the producers
of an equivalent amount (on a Btu basis) of dry natural gas.&nbsp; Generally,
the value of the NGLs extracted is greater than the cost of replacing those
Btus with dry gas, resulting in positive operating margins under these
contracts.&nbsp; Periodically, natural gas becomes more expensive, on a Btu
equivalent basis, than NGL products, and the cost of keeping the producer &#147;whole&#148;
can result in operating losses.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Debt</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
October 2004 the Company entered into a $25.0 million senior credit facility
with a term of one year.&nbsp; The $25.0 million revolving facility has a
variable interest rate based on the base rate or the London Inter Bank Offering
Rate (&#147;LIBOR&#148;), as discussed below.&#160; In
October, November and December 2005, the Company entered into the first, second
and third amendments to the credit agreement.&nbsp; The first amendment to the
credit facility extended the term of the original agreement to November 15,
2005.&nbsp; The second amendment reduced the lending amount from $25.0 million
to $16.0 million, of which $6.0 million is committed to a letter of credit,
leaving $10.0 million available for revolving loans.&nbsp; The second amendment
also extended the term of the revolving credit to December 30, 2005.&nbsp; The
third amendment extended the term of the revolving credit to January 31, 2006,
and reduced the lending amount from $16.0 million to $13.5 million, of which
$6.0 million is committed to a letter of credit, leaving $7.5 million available
for revolving loans. On January 31, 2006, the Company entered into the first
amended and restated credit agreement which reinstated the maximum lending
limit of $25.0 million for a one year term.&#160;
On August 18, 2006, the Company entered into the second amended and
restated credit facility which increased the size of the facility from $25
million to $55 million, increasing the term of the agreement to three years and
allowing the flexibility for MarkWest Hydrocarbon to directly invest in
additional units of MarkWest Energy Partners to fund future growth
opportunities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On February 16,
2007, the Company entered into the first amendment to the second amended and
restated credit agreement, increasing the term by one year to August&nbsp;20,
2010, and providing an additional $50&nbsp;million of credit to enable the
Company to meet margin requirements associated with its derivative instruments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company Credit Facility bears interest at a variable interest rate, plus basis
points.&nbsp; The variable interest rate typically is based on the LIBOR;
however, in certain borrowing circumstances the rate would be based on the
higher of a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5-1%, and b) a rate set by the
Facility&#146;s administrative agent, based on the U.S. prime rate.&#160; The basis points correspond to the ratio of
the Revolver Facility Usage to the Borrowing Base, ranging from 0.50% to 1.75%
for Base Rate loans, and 1.50% to 2.75% for Eurodollar Rate loans.&#160; The Company pays a quarterly commitment fee
on the unused portion of the credit facility at an annual rate ranging from
37.5 to 50.0 basis points.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
the provisions of the credit facility, the Company is subject to a number of
restrictions on its business, including its ability to grant liens on assets;
make or own certain investments; enter into any swap contracts other than in
the ordinary course of business; merge, consolidate or sell assets; incur
indebtedness (other than subordinated indebtedness); make distributions on
equity investments; declare or make, directly or indirectly, any restricted
distributions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At
December 31, 2006, we had no debt outstanding on the Company Credit Facility
and $28.0 million available for borrowing.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
spent $0.3 million for capital expenditures for the year ending December 31,
2006.&nbsp; We have budgeted $3.6 million for 2007, principally for computer
hardware and software upgrades.&nbsp; We believe that cash on hand, cash
received from quarterly distributions (including the incentive distribution
rights) from MarkWest Energy Partners and projected cash generated from our
marketing operations will be sufficient to meet our working capital
requirements and fund our required capital expenditures, if any, for the
foreseeable future.&nbsp; Cash generated from our marketing operations will
depend on our operating performance, which will be affected by prevailing
commodity prices and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership&#146;s primary source of liquidity to meet
operating expenses and fund capital expenditures (other than for certain
acquisitions) are cash flows generated by its operations and its access to
equity and debt markets. The equity and debt markets, public and private,
retail and institutional, have been the Partnership&#146;s principal source of
capital used to finance a significant amount of its growth, including
acquisitions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">On December&nbsp;29, 2005, MarkWest Energy Operating
Company, L.L.C., a wholly owned subsidiary of MarkWest Energy Partners L.P.,
entered into the fifth amended and restated credit agreement (&#147;Partnership
Credit Facility&#148;). It provides for a maximum lending limit of
$615.0&nbsp;million for a five-year term. The credit facility included a
revolving facility of $250.0&nbsp;million and a $365.0&nbsp;million term
loan.&#160; The term loan portion of the
Partnership Credit Facility was repaid without penalty in October 2006 using a
portion of the proceeds from the debt and equity offerings in 2006 leaving the
revolving facility intact. Under certain circumstances, the Partnership Credit
Facility can be increased from $250.0&nbsp;million up to $450.0&nbsp;million.
The credit facility is guaranteed by the Partnership and all of the
Partnership&#146;s subsidiaries and is collateralized by substantially all of the
Partnership&#146;s assets and those of its subsidiaries. The borrowings under the
credit facility bear interest at a variable interest rate, plus basis points.
The variable interest rate typically is based on the LIBOR; however, in certain
borrowing circumstances the rate would be based on the higher of a)&nbsp;the
Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5-1%, and b)&nbsp;a rate set by the Partnership
Credit Facility&#146;s administrative agent, based on the U.S. prime rate. The basis
points correspond to the ratio of the Partnership&#146;s Consolidated Senior Debt
(as defined in the Partnership Credit Facility) to Consolidated EBITDA (as
defined in the Partnership Credit Facility), ranging from 0.50% to 1.50% for
Base Rate loans, and 1.50% to 2.50% for Eurodollar Rate loans. The basis points
will increase by 0.50% during any period (not to exceed 270&nbsp;days) where
the Partnership makes an acquisition for a purchase price in excess of
$50.0&nbsp;million (&#147;Acquisition Adjustment Period&#148;). Borrowings under the Partnership
Credit Facility were used to finance, in part, the Javelina acquisition
discussed above. On December 31, 2006, the available borrowing capacity under
the Partnership Credit Facility was $218.4 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Cash generated from operations, borrowings under the
Partnership Credit Facility and funds from the Partnership&#146;s private and public
equity and debt offerings are its primary sources of liquidity. The timing of
the Partnership&#146;s efforts to raise equity in 2006 was influenced by its failure
to file in a timely manner its Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K for the year
ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, and its quarterly report on Form&nbsp;10-Q for
the quarter ending March&nbsp;31, 2005. However, as of October 11, 2006, the
Partnership has the ability to incorporate by reference information from its
future Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;) filings into new registration
statements in order to raise capital through a public offering.&#160; To raise additional capital through public
debt or equity offerings, the Partnership is eligible to file&nbsp;a
Form&nbsp;S-3, which is a short-form type of registration statement.&#160; On November 15, 2006, the Partnership filed a
shelf registration statement on Form S-3, which became effective immediately
and allows it to attempt to raise up to $500 million by issuing debt and equity
securities in the future in registered offerings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Partnership and its wholly
owned subsidiary MarkWest Energy Finance Corporation also</font></p>
