<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In February&nbsp;2006 the </font>F<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">ASB issued </font>SFAS No.<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;"> 155, <i>Accounting for Certain Hybrid Financial
Instruments&#151;an amendment of FASB Statements No.&nbsp;133 and 140</i> (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;155&#148;).
This statement amends <i>SFAS No. 133,
Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</i> (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;133&#148;),
and SFAS No.&nbsp;140, <i>Accounting for
Transfers and Servicing of Financial Assets and Extinguishments of Liabilities</i>
and resolves issues addressed in SFAS&nbsp;133 Implementation Issue No. D1, &#147;Application
of Statement 133 to Beneficial Interest in Securitized Financial Assets.&#148; This
Statement: (a)&nbsp;permits fair value remeasurement for any hybrid financial
instrument that contains an embedded derivative that otherwise would require bifurcation;
(b)&nbsp;clarifies which interest-only strips and principal-only strips are not
subject to the requirements of SFAS&nbsp;133; (c)&nbsp;establishes a
requirement to evaluate beneficial interests in securitized financial assets to
identify interests that are freestanding derivatives or that are hybrid
financial instruments that contain an embedded derivative requiring
bifurcation; (d)&nbsp;clarifies that concentrations of credit risk in the form
of subordination are not embedded derivatives; and, (e)&nbsp;eliminates restrictions
on a qualifying special-purpose entity&#146;s ability to hold passive
derivative financial instruments that pertain to beneficial interests that are
or contain a derivative financial instrument. The standard also requires
presentation within the financial statements that identifies those hybrid
financial instruments for which the fair value election has been applied and
information on the income statement impact of the changes in fair value of
those instruments. The Company is required to apply SFAS&nbsp;155 to all
financial instruments acquired, issued or subject to a remeasurement event
beginning January&nbsp;1, 2007, although early adoption is permitted as of the
beginning of an entity&#146;s fiscal year.</font>&#160;
The adoption of SFAS 155 is not expected to have a material impact on
the consolidated financial statements of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="background:white;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June 2006 the FASB issued Interpretation No. 48, <i>Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes </i>(&#147;FIN
48&#148;). The interpretation clarifies the accounting for uncertainty in income
taxes recognized in a company&#146;s financial statements in accordance with
SFAS109, <i>Accounting for Income Taxes</i>.
Specifically, the pronouncement prescribes a &#147;more likely than not&#148; recognition
threshold and a measurement attribute for the financial statement recognition
and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax
return. The interpretation also provides guidance on the related derecognition,
classification, interest and penalties, accounting for interim periods,
disclosure and transition of uncertain tax positions. The interpretation is
effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2006.&#160; The Company is currently evaluating the
impact of FIN 48.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September 2006
the FASB issued SFAS No.&nbsp;157, <i>Fair
Value Measurements </i>(&#147;SFAS 157&#148;). SFAS 157 clarifies the principle
that fair value should be based on the assumptions market participants would
use when pricing an asset or liability and establishes a fair value hierarchy
that prioritizes the information used to develop those assumptions. SFAS 157 is
effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning after
November&nbsp;15, 2007 and interim periods within those fiscal years, with
early adoption permitted.&#160; The Company
has not yet determined the impact, if any, the implementation of SFAS 157 may
have on the consolidated financial statements of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September 2006,
the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;) issued Staff Accounting Bulletin
No. 108, &#147;Considering the Effects of Prior Year Misstatements when Quantifying
Misstatements in Current Year Financial Statements&#148; (&#147;SAB 108&#148;). SAB 108
provides interpretive guidance on how the effects of the carryover or reversal
of prior year misstatements should be considered in quantifying a current year
misstatement. The SEC staff believes that registrants should quantify errors
using both a balance sheet and an income statement approach and evaluate
whether either approach results in quantifying a misstatement that, when all
relevant quantitative and qualitative factors are considered, is material. SAB
108 is effective for the first annual period ending after November 15, 2006.
The Company adopted SAB 108 for the</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">67</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">year ending December 31,
2006, and it did not have a material effect on the consolidated financial
statements of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The FASB has
issued SFAS No. 159,<i> The Fair Value Option
for Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities </i>(&#147;SFAS 159&#148;), which permits an entity
to measure certain financial assets and financial liabilities at fair value.
The Statement&#146;s objective is to improve financial reporting by allowing
entities to mitigate volatility in reported earnings caused by the measurement
of related assets and liabilities using different attributes, without having to
apply complex hedge accounting provisions. Under SFAS 159, entities that elect
the fair value option will report unrealized gains and losses in earnings at
each subsequent reporting date. The fair value option may be elected on an
instrument-by-instrument basis, with a few exceptions, as long as it is applied
to the instrument in its entirety. The fair value option election is
irrevocable, unless a new election date occurs. The new Statement establishes
presentation and disclosure requirements to help financial statement users
understand the effect of the entity&#146;s election on its earnings, but does not
eliminate disclosure requirements of other accounting standards. Assets and
liabilities that are measured at fair value must be displayed on the face of
the balance sheet. SFAS 159 is effective as of the beginning of an entity&#146;s
first fiscal year beginning after November 15, 2007. Early adoption is
permitted as of the beginning of the previous fiscal year provided that the
entity (1) makes that choice in the first 120 days of that fiscal year, (2) has
not yet issued financial statements, and (3) elects to apply the provisions of
SFAS 157. The Company has not yet determined the impact, if any; the
implementation of SFAS 159 may have on the consolidated financial statements of
the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">3.</font></i></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b style="font-style:normal;">Acquisitions by MarkWest Energy Partners</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2006, 2005
and 2004, the Partnership completed the following acquisitions. Each
acquisition was accounted for under the purchase method.&#160; The assets acquired and liabilities assumed
were recorded at the estimated fair market values as of the acquisition date.
The preliminary allocation of assets and liabilities may be adjusted to reflect
the final determined amounts during a short period of time following the
acquisition. The results of operations from these acquisitions are included in
our consolidated financial statements from the acquisition date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Santa
Fe Acquisition</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December 29, 2006, the
Partnership purchased 100% of the ownership interest in Santa Fe Gathering,
L.L.C for $15.0 million, subject to working capital adjustments.&#160; The gathering system is located in Roger
Mills and Beckham Counties, Oklahoma.&#160;
The Grimes system was constructed in May 2005 to gather from growing production
fields.&#160; Current system throughput is
approximately 16 MMcf/d.&#160; The final purchase
price allocation is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2007.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:2.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Javelina
Acquisition</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">On November&nbsp;1, 2005, the Partnership acquired equity
interests in Javelina Company, Javelina Pipeline Company and Javelina Land
Company, L.L.C., which were 40%, 40% and 20%, respectively, owned by
subsidiaries of El Paso Corporation, Kerr-McGee Corporation and Valero Energy
Corporation. The Partnership paid consideration of $357.0&nbsp;million, plus
$41.8&nbsp;million for net working capital that included approximately
$35.5&nbsp;million in cash. The Corpus Christi, Texas, gas processing facility
treats and processes off-gas from six local refineries, two of which are owned
by Valero Energy Corporation, two by Koch Industries,&nbsp;Inc. and two by
Citgo Petroleum Corporation. Constructed in 1989 to recover up to 28,000 Bbl/d
of NGLs, the facility currently processes approximately 125 to 130 MMcf/d of
inlet gas and produces approximately 26,200 Bbl/d of NGLs. The Partnership and
the seller negotiated a final settlement of the acquired working capital of
$41.8&nbsp;million, and the final payment of $5.9&nbsp;million was paid to the
sellers in May of 2006 and included in the final purchase price allocation,
which was completed in the second quarter of 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Starfish Joint Venture</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March 31, 2005, the Partnership paid $41.7 million
to an affiliate of Enterprise Products Partners L.P. for a 50% non-operating
membership interest in Starfish Pipeline Company, LLC.&#160; Starfish is a joint venture with Enbridge
Offshore Pipelines LLC, which the Partnership accounts for using the equity
method. Starfish owns the FERC-regulated Stingray natural gas pipeline, and the
unregulated Triton natural gas gathering system and West Cameron dehydration
facility. All are located in the Gulf of Mexico and southwestern Louisiana.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On

assets consist of processing plants, gathering systems, a processing facility
currently under construction and an NGL pipeline.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Hobbs</font></i><i> Lateral Acquisition</i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:35.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;">On April&nbsp;1,

consisted of a four-mile pipeline, with a capacity of 160 million cubic feet of
natural gas per day, connecting the Northern Natural Gas interstate pipeline to
Southwestern Public Service&#146;s Cunningham and Maddox power-generating stations
in Hobbs, New Mexico.&#160; The Hobbs lateral
is a New Mexico intrastate pipeline regulated by the FERC.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Pro
Forma Results of Operations (Unaudited)</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table reflects the
unaudited pro forma consolidated results of operations for the years ended
December 31, 2005 and 2004, as though the Javelina, Starfish and East Texas
acquisitions had occurred on January 1, 2004. The unaudited pro forma results
of operations for the Hobbs and Santa Fe acquisitions have not been presented,
as the acquisitions were not considered significant.&#160; The results have been prepared for
comparative purposes only and may not be indicative of future results.&#160; </font>All earnings per share information have been updated to
reflect the May 2006 stock dividend.</p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">4. Marketable securities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Marketable
securities are classified as available-for-sale and stated at market based on
the closing price of the securities at the balance sheet date.&nbsp;
Accordingly, unrealized gains are reflected in other comprehensive income, net
of applicable income taxes.&nbsp; For losses that are other than temporary, the
cost basis of the securities is written down to fair value, and the amount of
the write down is reflected in the statement of operations.&#160; The Company utilizes a first-in first-out
cost basis to compute realized gains and losses.&nbsp; Realized gains and
losses, dividends, interest income, and the amortization of discounts and
premiums are reflected in the statement of operations.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">69</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended
December 31, 2006, the Company recognized net unrealized gains on marketable
securities of $0.7 million, net of the related tax expense of $0.5
million.&#160; These gains are shown as a
component of other comprehensive income for 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended
December 31, 2005, the Company recognized net unrealized losses on marketable
securities of $0.2 million, net of the related tax benefit of $0.1
million.&#160; These losses are shown as a
component of other comprehensive income for 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">5.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Significant
Customers and Concentration of Credit
Risk</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended
December 31, 2006, revenues from Targa Resources Partners, L.P. (&#147;Targa&#148;)
totaled $76 million, representing 10% of the Company&#146;s consolidated
revenues.&#160; Sales to Targa are made
primarily from the MarkWest Energy Partner segment.&#160; The Company had a receivable of $3.0 million
from Targa as of December 31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years
ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, revenues from one other customer totaled $67
million and $60 million, representing 9% and 13% of the Company&#146;s consolidated
revenues, respectively.&#160; Sales to this
customer were made primarily from the MarkWest Energy Partner segment.&#160; The Company had a receivable of $5.5 million
from this customer as of December 31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Risk management premium</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the third and fourth quarters of 2006 the
Partnership entered into certain put option contracts on commodities requiring
premium payments to secure certain floor prices.&#160; The Partnership paid $1.0 million to the
counterparty as a premium on certain short-term put option contracts.&#160; The payment is recorded as a short-term asset
and will be amortized through revenue as the puts expire or are exercised.&#160; The contracts are recorded as derivative
instruments, so charges in fair value of the contracts are recorded as an
unrelated gain or loss.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">7.&#160; Properties, plant and equipment</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Property, plant and equipment consist of (in
thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company capitalizes interest on major projects during construction.&#160; For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006
and 2005, the Company capitalized interest of $0.9 million and $2.1 million,
respectively</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Woodford gathering system</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In late 2006 the
Partnership began the construction and operation of the Woodford gathering
system and compression system to support wells in a 200-square-mile project
area situated in a four-county region in the Arkoma Basin in eastern Oklahoma.
As of December 31, 2006, the Partnership invested capital of $26.4 million.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">8.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b>Intangible
assets</b></p>

2006 and 2005 are comprised of customer contracts and relationships, as follows
(in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Risk management premium</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In the third and fourth quarters of 2006 the Partnership
entered into certain put option contracts on commodities requiring premium
payments to secure certain floor prices.&#160;
The Partnership paid $0.7 million to the counterparty as a premium on
certain long-term put option contracts.&#160;
The payment is recorded as a long-term asset (and reclassified to a
current asset once the contract is set to expire within one year) and will be
amortized through revenue as the puts expire or are exercised.&#160; The contracts are recorded as derivative instruments,
so changes in fair value of the contracts are recorded as an unrealized gain or
loss.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">10.</font></i></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b style="font-style:normal;">Accrued liabilities</b></p>

thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">11.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Asset retirement obligation</b></p>

<p align="left" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">The Company adopted Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards No. 143, <i>Accounting
for Asset Retirement Obligations </i>(&#147;SFAS 143&#148;)<i>,</i> on
January&nbsp;1, 2003. Under SFAS 143, the fair value of a liability for an
asset retirement obligation is recognized in the period in which the liability
is incurred with an offsetting increase in the carrying amount of the related
long-lived asset. </font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">The recognition of an asset
retirement obligation requires that management make numerous estimates,
assumptions and judgments regarding such factors as the estimated
probabilities, amounts and timing of settlements; the credit-adjusted risk-free
rate to be used; inflation rates, and future advances in technology.&#160; In periods subsequent to initial measurement
of the liability, we must recognize period-to-period changes in the liability
resulting from the passage of time and revisions to either the timing or the
amount of the original estimate of undiscounted cash flows.</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">  </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">Over time, the liability is
accreted to its future value, and the capitalized cost is depreciated over the
useful life of the related asset. Upon settlement of the liability, an entity
either settles the obligation for its recorded amount or incurs a gain or loss.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company&#146;s assets subject to asset retirement obligations are primarily certain
gas-gathering pipelines and processing facilities, a crude oil pipeline and
other related pipeline assets.&#160; The
Company also has land leases that require the Company to return the land to its
original condition upon the termination of the lease.&#160;&#160; In connection with the adoption of SFAS 143,
the Company reviewed current laws and regulations governing obligations for
asset retirements and leases, as well as the Company&#146;s leases and other
agreements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a reconciliation of the changes in
the asset retirement obligation from December 31, 2004, to December&nbsp;31,
2006 (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Credit Facility (August 2006 to Present)</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August 18,
2006, the Company entered into the second amended and restated credit agreement
(&#147;Company Credit Facility&#148;) which provides a maximum lending limit of $55.0
million, increased from $25.0 million; and extends the term from one to three
years.&#160; The Company Credit Facility
includes a $40.0 million Revolving Facility and a $15.0 million Unit
Acquisition Facility. The $15.0 million Unit Acquisition Facility may be used
to finance the acquisition of MarkWest Energy Partners common or subordinated
units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company Credit
Facility bears interest at a variable interest rate, plus basis points.&nbsp;
The variable interest rate typically is based on the London Inter Bank Offering
Rate (&#147;LIBOR&#148;); however, in certain borrowing circumstances the rate would be
based on the higher of a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5-1%, and b) a rate set
by the Facility&#146;s administrative agent, based on the U.S. prime rate.&#160; The basis points correspond to the ratio of
the Revolver Facility Usage to the Borrowing Base, ranging from 0.50% to 1.75%
for Base Rate loans, and 1.50% to 2.75% for Eurodollar Rate loans.&#160; The Company pays a quarterly commitment fee
on the unused portion of the credit facility at an annual rate ranging from
37.5 to 50.0 basis points.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the
provisions of the Company Credit Facility, the Company is subject to a number
of restrictions on its business, including its ability to grant liens on
assets; make or own certain investments; enter into any swap contracts other
than in the ordinary course of business; merge, consolidate or sell assets;
incur indebtedness (other than subordinated indebtedness); make distributions on
equity investments; declare or make, directly or indirectly, any restricted
distributions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The credit
facility also contains covenants requiring the Company to maintain:</font></p>

collateral coverage ratio of not more than 2.0 to 1.0 as of the date of any

Non-Borrowing Base Revolving Credit Facility (&#147;NBB Facility&#148;). The NBB Facility
provides for up to $50&nbsp;million of credit to enable the Company to meet

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Credit Facility (January 2006 to August 2006)</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
January 31, 2006, the Company entered into the first amended and restated
credit agreement, which provided a maximum lending limit of $25.0 million for a
one-year term, and which amended and restated the October 2004 agreement discussed
below. As of December 31, 2006, the Company had $6.0 million of the
availability committed to a letter of credit, leaving $19.0 million available
for revolving loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
March 23, 2006, the Company amended the First Amended and Restated Credit
Agreement to reduce the cash reserve requirement from $13.0 million to $5.0
million through December 31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Credit Facility (October 2004 to January 2006)</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
October 2004 the Company entered into a $25.0 million senior credit facility
with a term of one year.&nbsp; The $25.0 million revolving facility had a
variable interest rate based on the base rate, which is equal to the higher of
a) the Federal Funds Rate plus &#189; of 1%, and b) the rate of interest in effect
for such day as publicly announced from time to time by the Administrative
Agent as its prime rate, plus the applicable rate, which is based on a
utilization percentage.&nbsp; In October, November and December 2005, the
Company entered into the first, second and third amendment to the credit
agreement.&nbsp; The first amendment extended the term of the original
agreement to November 15, 2005.&nbsp; The second amendment reduced the lending
amount from $25.0 million to $16.0 million, of which $6.0 million of
availability is committed to a letter of credit, leaving $10.0 million
available for revolving loans.&nbsp; The second amendment also extended the
term of the revolving credit to December 30, 2005.&nbsp; The third amendment
extended the term of the revolving credit to January 31, 2006, and reduced the
lending amount from $16.0 million to $13.5 million, of which $6.0 million is
committed to a letter of credit, leaving $7.5 million available for revolving
loans at December 31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">2016 Senior Notes</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In July&nbsp;2006 MarkWest Energy Partners, LP and its
wholly owned subsidiary MarkWest Energy Finance Corporation (the &#147;Issuers&#148;)
co-issued $200&nbsp;million in aggregate principal amount of 8</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">1</font><font face="Symbol" style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#164;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;position:relative;top:1.0pt;">2</font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">% senior notes due 2016 (the &#147;2016 Senior Notes&#148;)
to qualified institutional buyers. The 2016 Senior Notes will mature on
July&nbsp;15, 2016, and interest is payable on each July&nbsp;15 and
January&nbsp;15, commencing January&nbsp;15, 2007.&#160; In October 2006 the Issuers offered </font>$75.0
million in <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">additional </font>debt securities
under this same indenture. <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The net proceeds
from the private placements were approximately $191.2&nbsp;million and $74.5
million, respectively, after deducting the initial purchasers&#146; discounts and
legal, accounting and other transaction expenses. The Issuers used a portion of
the net proceeds from the offerings to repay the term debt under the
Partnership Credit Facility. Affiliates of several of the initial purchasers,
including RBC Capital Markets Corporation, J.P. Morgan Securities&nbsp;Inc.,
and Wachovia Capital Markets, LLC, are lenders under the Partnership Credit
Facility.&#160; Each of the Partnership&#146;s
existing subsidiaries, other than MarkWest Energy Finance Corporation, has
guaranteed the notes jointly and severally and fully and unconditionally.&#160; The 2016 notes are senior unsecured
obligations equal in right of payment with all of the Partnership&#146;s existing
and future senior debt.&#160; These notes are
senior in right of payment to all of the Partnership&#146;s future subordinated debt
but effectively junior in right of payment to its secured debt to the extent of
the assets securing the debt, including the Partnership&#146;s obligations in
respect of its Partnership Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The indenture governing the Partnership&#146;s 2016 Senior
Notes limits the activity of the Partnership and its restricted subsidiaries,
including the ability of the Partnership and its restricted subsidiaries to
incur additional indebtedness; declare or pay dividends or distributions, or
redeem, repurchase or retire equity interests or subordinated indebtedness;
make investments; incur liens; create any consensual limitation on the ability
of the Partnership&#146;s restricted subsidiaries to pay dividends, make loans or
transfer property to the Partnership; engage in transactions with the
Partnership&#146;s affiliates; sell assets, including equity interests of the
Partnership&#146;s subsidiaries; make any payment on or with respect to, or
purchase, redeem, defease or otherwise acquire or retire for value any
subordinated obligation or guarantor subordination obligation (except principal
and interest at maturity); and consolidate, merge or transfer assets. Subject
to compliance with certain covenants, the Partnership may issue additional
notes from time to time under the indenture pursuant to Rule&nbsp;144A and
Regulation&nbsp;S under the Securities Act of 1933.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">2014 Senior Notes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
October 2004 MarkWest Energy Partners, LP and its wholly owned subsidiary,
MarkWest Energy Finance Corporation, co-issued $225.0 million in senior notes (&#147;2014
Senior Notes&#148;) at a fixed rate of 6.875%, payable semi-annually in arrears on
May 1 and November 1, and commencing on May 1, 2005. The 2014 Senior Notes
mature on November&nbsp;1, 2014. The Partnership may redeem some or all of the
notes at any time on or after November&nbsp;1, 2009, at certain redemption
prices together with accrued and unpaid
interest to the date of redemption. The Partnership may redeem all of the notes
at any time prior to November&nbsp;1, 2009, at a make-whole redemption price.
In addition, prior to November&nbsp;1, 2007, the Partnership may redeem up to
35% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes with the proceeds of certain
equity offerings at a stated redemption price. The Partnership must offer to
repurchase the notes at a specified price if it a) sells certain assets and
does not reinvest the proceeds or repay senior indebtedness, or b) experiences
specific kinds of changes in control.&#160;
Each of the Partnership&#146;s existing subsidiaries, other than MarkWest
Energy Finance Corporation, has guaranteed the notes jointly and severally and
fully and unconditionally.&#160; The 2014
Senior Notes are senior unsecured obligations equal in right of payment with
all of the Partnership&#146;s existing and future senior debt.&#160; These notes are senior in right of payment to
all of the Partnership&#146;s future subordinated debt but effectively junior in
right of payment to its secured debt to the extent of the assets securing the
debt, including the Partnership&#146;s obligations in respect of its Partnership
Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The indenture governing the 2014 Senior Notes limits the
activity of the Partnership and its restricted subsidiaries. Limitations
include the ability of the Partnership and its restricted subsidiaries to incur
additional indebtedness; declare or pay dividends or distributions, or redeem,
repurchase or retire equity interests or subordinated indebtedness; make
investments; incur liens; create any consensual limitation on the ability of
the Partnership&#146;s restricted subsidiaries to pay dividends, make loans or
transfer property to the Partnership; engage in transactions with the
Partnership&#146;s affiliates; sell assets, including equity interests of the
Partnership&#146;s subsidiaries; make any payment on or with respect to, or purchase,
redeem, defease or otherwise acquire or retire for value any subordinated
obligation or guarantor subordination obligation (except principal and interest
at maturity); and consolidate, merge or transfer assets. Subject to compliance
with certain covenants, the Partnership may issue additional notes from time to
time under the indenture pursuant to Rule&nbsp;144A and Regulation&nbsp;S under
the Securities Act of 1933.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Partnership agreed to file an exchange offer registration statement or, under
certain circumstances, a shelf registration statement, pursuant to a
registration rights agreement relating to the 2014 Senior Notes. The
Partnership failed to complete the exchange offer in the time provided for in
the subscription agreements (April&nbsp;26, 2005) and, as a consequence, was
incurring an interest rate penalty of 0.5% annually, increasing 0.25% every 90
days thereafter up to 1%, until such time as the exchange offer was completed.
The registration statement was filed on January 17, 2006, the exchange offer was
completed on March 7, 2006, and the interest penalty ceased.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:15.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Partnership Credit Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
December&nbsp;29, 2005, MarkWest Energy Operating Company, L.L.C., a wholly
owned subsidiary of MarkWest Energy Partners L.P., entered into the fifth
amended and restated credit agreement (&#147;Partnership Credit Facility&#148;), which
provides for a maximum lending limit of $615.0 million for a five-year
term.&nbsp; The credit facility includes a revolving facility of $250.0 million
and a $365.0 million term loan.&nbsp; The credit facility is guaranteed by the
Partnership and all of the Partnership&#146;s subsidiaries and is collateralized by
substantially all of the Partnership&#146;s assets and those of its
subsidiaries.&nbsp; The borrowings under the credit facility bear interest at a
variable interest rate, plus basis points.&nbsp; The basis points vary based on
the ratio of the Partnership&#146;s Consolidated Debt (as defined in the Partnership
Credit Facility) to Consolidated EBITDA (as defined in the Partnership Credit
Facility), ranging from 0.50% to 1.50% for Base Rate loans, and 1.50% to 2.50%
for Eurodollar Rate loans.&nbsp; The basis points will increase by 0.50% during
any period (not to exceed 270 days) where the Partnership makes an acquisition
for a purchase price in excess of $50.0 million (&#147;Acquisition Adjustment Period&#148;).
For the year ended December 31, 2006, the weighted average interest rate on the
Partnership Credit Facility was 7.2%.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">13.&#160; Derivative
financial instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our primary risk management objective is to manage
volatility in our cash flows.&nbsp; A committee comprised of members of the
senior management team oversees all of our derivative activity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We utilize a combination of
fixed-price forward contracts, fixed-for-floating price swaps and options on
the over-the-counter (&#147;OTC&#148;) market.&nbsp; The Company may also enter into
futures contracts traded on the New York Mercantile Exchange (&#147;NYMEX&#148;).&nbsp;
Swaps and futures contracts allow us to manage volatility in our margins
because corresponding losses or gains on the financial instruments are
generally offset by gains or losses in our physical positions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We enter into OTC swaps with financial institutions
and other energy company counterparties.&nbsp; We conduct a standard credit
review on counterparties and have agreements containing collateral requirements
where deemed necessary.&nbsp; We use standardized swap agreements that allow
for offset of positive and negative exposures.&nbsp; We may be subject to
margin deposit requirements under OTC agreements (with non-bank counterparties)
and NYMEX positions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The use of derivative instruments may expose us to the
risk of financial loss in certain circumstances, including instances when (i)
NGLs do not trade at historical levels relative to crude oil, (ii) sales
volumes are less than expected requiring market purchases to meet commitments,
or (iii) our OTC counterparties fail to purchase or deliver the contracted
quantities of natural gas, NGLs or crude oil or otherwise fail to perform. To
the extent that we enter into derivative instruments, we may be prevented from
realizing the benefits of favorable price changes in the physical market. We
are similarly insulated, however, against unfavorable changes in such prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value is based on available market information for the
particular derivative instrument and incorporates the commodity, period, volume
and pricing.&nbsp; Positive (negative) amounts represent unrealized gains
(losses).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Hydrocarbon Standalone</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">MarkWest
Hydrocarbon Standalone may enter into physical and/or financial positions to
manage its risks related to commodity price exposure.&nbsp; Due to timing of
purchases and sales, direct exposure to price volatility can be created because
there is no longer an offsetting purchase or sale that remains exposed to market
pricing.&nbsp; Through marketing and derivatives activities, direct exposure
may occur naturally, or we may choose direct exposure when we favor that
exposure over frac spread risk. Beginning in 2006 MarkWest Hydrocarbon
Standalone pre-purchased natural gas for shrink requirements in future months
and, for both natural gas and NGLs, entered into swaps and future sales
agreements to manage frac spread risk. These derivative instruments are marked
to market.</font></p>

tables summarize the current derivative positions specific to MarkWest
Hydrocarbon Standalone&#146;s segment at December 31, 2006 (in thousands, except
price data):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 72.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Swaps represent fixed forward sales and purchases, which, in combination
economically hedge our frac spread position.</p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy
Partners</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership&#146;s
primary risk management objective is to reduce volatility in its cash flows
arising from changes in commodity prices related to future sales of natural
gas, NGLs and crude oil.&nbsp; Swaps and futures contracts may allow the
Partnership to reduce volatility in its realized margins as realized losses or
gains on the derivative instruments generally are offset by corresponding gains
or losses in the Partnership&#146;s sales of physical product.&#160; While the Partnership largely expects it&#146;s
realized derivative gains and losses to be offset by increases or decreases in
the value of its physical sales, it will experience volatility in reported
earnings due to the recording of unrealized gains and losses on its derivative
positions that will have no offset.&#160; The
volatility in any given period related to unrealized gains or losses can be
significant to the overall results of the Partnership, however, it ultimately
expects those gains and losses to be offset when they become realized.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
tables summarize the current derivative positions specific to MarkWest Energy
Partner&#146;s segment at December 31, 2006 (in thousands, except price data):</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006 the
Company had state net operating loss carryforwards of approximately $14.6
million that expire between 2011 and 2026.&#160;
The Company expects that future taxable income will likely be
apportioned to states other than those in which the net operating loss was
generated.&#160; As a result, the Company
believes it is more likely than not that the state net operating losses will
not be realized and has provided a 100% valuation allowance against this
long-term deferred tax asset.&#160; The
Company had federal alternative minimum tax credit carryforwards of $2.7
million that have no expiration date and can be applied as a credit to reduce
regular federal income tax.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">15.</font></b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><b>Stock and Incentive Compensation Plans</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All previously
awarded MarkWest Hydrocarbon restricted stock, stock options and other
compensation arrangements based on the market value of our common stock have
been adjusted to reflect the May 2006 stock dividend.&#160; Furthermore, all previously awarded
Partnership units have been adjusted to reflect the February 2007 two-for-one
unit split (see Note 2 above).</font></p>

cost for share-based pay arrangements was as follows (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At
December 31, 2006, the Company has three stock-based compensation plans, one of
which is through its consolidated subsidiary, MarkWest Energy Partners.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">2006 Stock Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
June 2006, the Company&#146;s shareholders approved the 2006 Stock Incentive Plan (&#147;2006
Plan&#148;), effective July 1, 2006.&#160; The 2006
Plan replaced both the 1996 Stock Incentive Plan and the 1996 Non-employee
Director Stock Option Plan (together the &#147;1996 Plans&#148;).&#160; Under the 2006 Plan the Company may grant a
maximum of 1,000,000 restricted shares and stock options, subject to varying
vesting terms and expected terms as discussed below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock
Options</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company issued
stock options under the 1996 Plans until 2005. While it was determined in 2005
that the Company does not intend to issue stock options in the future, they are
available for issuance under the 2006 Plan.&#160;&#160;
On December 1, 2006 a board resolution provided for the accelerated
vesting of 14,950 unvested stock option grants affecting eight employees.&#160; Consequently, as of December 31, 2006 the
Company had no remaining unvested options or any unrecognized compensation
expense pertaining to options.&#160; For the
year ended December 31, 2006, the Company received $0.3 million from the exercise
of stock options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under SFAS 123R,
the Company&#146;s stock options are categorized as equity awards.&nbsp;
Accordingly, compensation expense for options is measured based on the grant
date fair value and is amortized into earnings over the service period as the
options vest.&#160; The options historically
vested at the rate of 25% per year for options granted in 1999 and thereafter,
and 20% per year for options granted prior to 1999.&#160; The fair value of the options is estimated
using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&nbsp; The options have a maximum
term of ten years and may, at the discretion of the Company, be exercised using
either a Company-assisted or broker-assisted cashless exercise.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
summarizes the impact of the Company&#146;s stock option plan (in thousands of
shares):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Stock</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.3pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company issued restricted stock under the 1996 Plans until the adoption of the
2006 Plan at which point all new shares are, and will be, issued pursuant to
the rules of the 2006 Plan.&#160; Under SFAS
123R, the restricted stock qualifies as an equity award.&#160; Accordingly, restricted stock is measured at
the grant date fair value and the associated compensation expense is recognized
over the requisite service period, reduced for an estimate of expected
forfeitures.&#160; The restricted stock vests
equally over a three year period.&#160; No
shares were granted prior to 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
summarizes the impact of the Company&#146;s restricted stock plans:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
the years ended December 31, 2006, 2005 and 2004, the Company received no
proceeds for issuing restricted stock, and there were no cash settlements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Participation Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company has also entered into arrangements with certain directors and employees
of the Company referred to as the Participation Plan.&nbsp; Under it, the
Company sells subordinated units of the Partnership or interests in the
Partnership&#146;s general partner under a purchase and sale agreement.&nbsp; There
is no maximum contractual term under the Participation Plan. The Company&#146;s
capacity to grant further general partner interests is limited by its ownership
in the general partner.&#160; The subordinated
units are sold without any restrictions on transfer.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Both the
subordinated unit and general partner interest transactions are considered
compensatory arrangements due to the put-and-call provisions and the associated
valuation being based on a formula instead of an independent third party
valuation. Under SFAS 123R, the subordinated units and general partner
interests are classified as liability awards.&#160;
As a result, the Company is required to mark to market the subordinated
unit and general partner interest valuations at the end of each period.&#160; Compensation expense related to general
partner interests is calculated as the difference in the formula value and the
amount paid by those individuals.&nbsp; The formula value is the amount
MarkWest Hydrocarbon would have to pay the employees and directors to
repurchase the general partner interests, and is based on the current market
value of the Partnership&#146;s common units and the current quarterly distributions
paid.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The interest in
the Partnership&#146;s general partner is sold with certain put-and-call
provisions.&#160; These require MarkWest
Hydrocarbon to buy back, or require the individuals to sell back their interest
in the general partner to MarkWest Hydrocarbon.&nbsp; Specifically, the employees
and directors can exercise their put if (1)&nbsp;MarkWest Hydrocarbon or the
Partnership&#146;s general partner undergoes a change of control;
(2)&nbsp;additional membership interests are issued that, on a pro forma basis,
decrease the distributions to all the then existing members; (3)&nbsp;any
amendment, alteration or repeal of the provisions of the general partner
agreement materially and adversely affects the then existing rights, duties,
obligations or restrictions of the employees and directors; or (4)&nbsp;the
employee or director (i)&nbsp;becomes totally disabled while a director,
officer or employee of the general partner, of MarkWest Hydrocarbon or of any
of their affiliates, or (ii)&nbsp;dies, or (iii)&nbsp;retires as a director,
officer or employee of the general partner of MarkWest Hydrocarbon or of any of
their affiliates after reaching the age of 60 years.&nbsp; The employee or his
estate has 120 days after the put event to exercise the put under (4)&nbsp;and
30 days after notice to exercise under (1)&nbsp;through (3).&nbsp;MarkWest
Hydrocarbon can exercise its call option if (i) the employee or director ceases
to be a director or employee of MarkWest Hydrocarbon or any of its affiliates,
or (ii) if there is a change of control of MarkWest or of the Partnership&#146;s
general partner. For the call option based upon a termination of employment or
directorship, MarkWest Hydrocarbon has 12 months following the termination date
to exercise its call option. MarkWest Hydrocarbon has agreed to exempt the
general partner interests of three present or former directors from the call
option based upon a termination of employment or directorship.&#160; Additionally, pursuant to the terms of our
current CEO&#146;s employment agreement with MarkWest Hydrocarbon, all of his
general partner interest has become exempt from the call option based upon a
termination of employment or directorship for reasons other than cause. For the
call option based upon a change of control of MarkWest or of the Partnership&#146;s
general partner, MarkWest Hydrocarbon has 30 days following the change of
control to exercise its call option.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October 13,
2006, the Company completed the repurchase&nbsp;of a 0.5% interest in the
general partner.&#160; This purchase resulted
in an increase in our ownership level in the general partner to 89.7%.&#160; The Company did not sell any subordinated
units to employees or directors in 2006 or 2005.&nbsp; Likewise, the Company
did not reacquire any subordinated units in 2006 or 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners&#146; Long-Term Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The number of
restricted units available for issuance under the LTIP has been adjusted to
reflect the February 2007 two-for-one unit split (see Note 2 above).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
general partner has adopted the MarkWest Energy Partners, L.P. Long-Term
Incentive Plan for employees and directors of the general partner, as well as
employees of its affiliates who perform services for us. The plan consists of</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">84</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">restricted units and
unit options. It permits the grant of awards covering an aggregate of 1,000,000
common units, comprised of 400,000 restricted units and 600,000 unit options.
The Compensation Committee of the general partner&#146;s Board of Directors
administers the plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Restricted Units</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A
restricted unit is a &#147;phantom&#148; unit that entitles the grantee to receive a
common unit of the Partnership upon the vesting of the phantom unit, or, at the
discretion of the Compensation Committee, cash equivalent to the value of a
common unit.&nbsp; The restricted units vest over a service period of three
years; however, vesting for certain awards may be accelerated if specific
annualized distribution goals are met. During the vesting period, these
restricted units are entitled to receive distribution equivalents, which
represent cash equal to the amount of distributions made on common units.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under
SFAS 123R, the restricted units are treated as liability awards.&#160; As a
result, the Partnership is required to mark to market the awards at the end of
each reporting period.&#160; Compensation
expense is measured for the phantom unit grants using the market price of
MarkWest Energy Partners&#146; common units at each reporting date. The fair value
of the units awarded is amortized into earnings over the period of service and
is adjusted monthly for the change in the fair value of the unvested units
granted.</font></p>

following is a summary of restricted unit activity under the Partnership&#146;s
Long-Term Incentive Plan:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the year ended
December 31, 2006, the Partnership issued 26,986 common units for vested
restricted units.&#160; For the years ended
December 31, 2005 and 2004 the partnership issued 17,700 and 54,596 common
units, respectively and an additional 500 units were acquired in the open
market in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the total
number of restricted units that vested in 2006, 2005 and 2004, the Partnership
received no proceeds for issuing restricted units (other than the contributions
by the general partner to maintain its 2% ownership interest), and there were
no cash settlements.&#160; Additionally, in
2004 the Partnership&#146;s opted to redeem 310 restricted units for cash.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Unit Options<b>.</b>&nbsp;</font></i><font face="Times New Roman">The
Compensation Committee has the authority to make grants of unit options under
the plan to employees and directors containing such terms as the committee
shall determine. Unit options are exercisable over a period determined by the
Compensation Committee. Unit options also are exercisable upon a change in
control of the Partnership, the general partner, MarkWest Hydrocarbon or upon
the achievement of specified financial objectives.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December 31, 2006,
the Partnership had not granted any unit options.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">16.</font></b><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font style="font-weight:bold;">Employee</font> Benefit Plan</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company made contributions of $1.0 million, $1.0 million and $0.5 million to a
401(k) savings and profit-sharing plan for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively. The Company did not contribute any common
shares to a 401(k) savings or profit-sharing plan for the year ended December
31, 2006.&#160; The Company contributed
approximately 12,000 and 15,000 common shares to a 401(k) savings and
profit-sharing plan for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004,
respectively, with an aggregate fair value of $1.0 million and $0.2 million,
respectively.&nbsp; The plan is discretionary, with annual contributions
determined by the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">17.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Stockholder&#146;s equity</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock Dividends</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
April 27, 2006, MarkWest Hydrocarbon announced that its Board of Directors
approved the issuance of one share of common stock for each ten shares of
common stock held by common stockholders. The stock was issued on May 23, 2006,
to the stockholders of record as of the close of business on May 11, 2006; the
ex-dividend date was May 9, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
October&nbsp;28, 2004, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors declared a stock
dividend of one share of MarkWest Hydrocarbon&#146;s common stock for each ten
shares owned by stockholders.&nbsp; The stock dividend of 976,974 shares was
paid on November&nbsp;19, 2004 to the stockholders of record as of the close of
business on November&nbsp;9, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash Dividend</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
January&nbsp;22, 2004, the Board of Directors declared a one-time special cash
dividend of $0.50 per share of common stock.&nbsp; The dividend was paid on
February&nbsp;18, 2004 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on
February&nbsp;4, 2004, with an ex-dividend date of February&nbsp;2, 2004.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">MarkWest Energy Partners</font></i></b></p>

on February 22, 2007 received one additional Common Unit for each Common Unit
owned on that date.&#160; The unit split
resulted in the issuance of an additional 15,603,257 common units and 600,000</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Public Offering </font>&#150; July 6, 2006</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:35.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Partnership priced its offering of 6,000,000

general partner to maintain its 2% general partner interest in the Partnership,
to repay a portion of the outstanding indebtedness under term debt on the
Partnership Credit Facility.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Private Placement &#150;

were received in December&nbsp;2005.&#160; The

$0.1 million reduced the aggregate gross proceeds of $25.0 million to $24.9
million of net proceeds.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Private Placement &#150;

reduced the aggregate gross proceeds of $72.7 million to $72.6 million of net

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Public Offering &#150; September&nbsp;21,
2004</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The

The Partnership sold 4,000,000 units, for gross proceeds of $86.8 million. The
remaining 314,790 were sold by certain unitholders, who retained the proceeds. </font>In connection with the over-allotment

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Private Placement &#150; July&nbsp;30,

<h6 style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:20.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Public Offering </font>&#150;</font></i><i> January&nbsp;12, 2004</i></h6>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">18.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Commitments and
contingencies</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:18.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Legal</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the ordinary
course of its business the Company is subject to a variety of risks and
disputes normal to its business and as a party to various legal proceedings. We
maintain insurance policies in amounts and with coverage and deductibles as we
believe are reasonable and prudent. However, we cannot assure either that the
insurance companies will promptly honor their policy obligations or that the
coverage or levels of insurance will be adequate to protect us from all
material expenses related to future claims for property loss or business
interruption to the Company; or for third-party claims of personal and
property damage; or that the coverages or levels of insurance it currently has
will be available in the future at economical prices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">87</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2005 MarkWest
Hydrocarbon,&nbsp;the Partnership, several of its affiliates, and an unrelated
co-defendant, were served with three lawsuits, which in 2006 were consolidated
into a single action captioned <i>Ricky J.
Conn, et al. v. MarkWest Hydrocarbon,&nbsp;Inc. et al.,</i> Floyd
Circuit Court, Commonwealth of Kentucky, and Civil Action No.&nbsp;05-CI-00137
(consolidated March 27, 2006 of three cases originally filed February,
2005).&#160; These actions involved third-party
claims of property and personal injury damages sustained as a consequence of an
NGL pipeline leak and an ensuing explosion and fire that occurred on
November&nbsp;8, 2004 in Ivel Kentucky. The pipeline was owned by an unrelated
business entity, Equitable Production Company, and leased and operated by the
Partnership&#146;s subsidiary, MarkWest Energy Appalachia, LLC (&#147;MEA&#148;). MEA
transports NGLs from the Maytown gas processing plant to MEA&#146;s Siloam
fractionator. The explosion and fire from the leaked vapors resulted in
property damage to several residential structures and injuries to some of the
residents.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The Company notified its general liability insurance
carriers of the incident and the lawsuits in a timely manner and coordinated
its legal defense with the insurers. As of February 1, 2007, all of the claims
in the litigation were fully settled, with MarkWest&#146;s insurance carrier and its
co-defendant and its separate insurance carrier, funding the settlements</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">In June&nbsp;2006, a Notice of Probable Violation and
Proposed Civil Penalty (NOPV) (CPF No. 2-2006-5001) was issued by OPS to both
MarkWest Hydrocarbon and Equitable Production Company, the owner of the
pipeline, asserting six counts of violations of applicable regulations, and a
proposed civil penalty in the aggregate amount of $1,070,000. An administrative
hearing on the matter is presently set for the last week of March, 2007.&#160; One of the counts of violations, which count
involves $825,000 of the $1,070,000
proposed penalty, concerns alleged activity in 1982 and 1987, which dates
predate MarkWest&#146;s leasing and operation of the pipeline.&#160; MarkWest believes it has viable defenses to
the remaining counts and will </font>vigorously defend all applicable
assertions of violations at the hearing.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Related to the above referenced pipeline incident,
MarkWest Hydrocarbon and the Partnership have filed an independent action
captioned <i>MarkWest Hydrocarbon,&nbsp;Inc.,
et al. v. Liberty Mutual Ins. Co., et al.</i> (District Court, Arapahoe
County, Colorado, Case No.&nbsp;05CV3953 filed August&nbsp;12, 2005), as
removed to the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, (Civil Action
No.&nbsp;1:05-CV-1948, on October&nbsp;7, 2005) against its All-Risks Property
and Business Interruption insurance carriers as a result of the insurance
companies&#146; refusal to honor their insurance coverage obligation to pay the
Company for certain expenses related to the pipeline incident. These include
the Company&#146;s internal expenses and costs incurred for damage to, and loss of
use of the pipeline, equipment and products; the extra transportation costs
incurred for transporting the liquids while the pipeline was out of service;
the reduced volumes of liquids that could be processed; and the costs of
complying with the OPS Corrective Action Order (hydrostatic testing,
repair/replacement and other pipeline integrity assurance measures). These
expenses and costs have been expensed as incurred and any potential recovery
from the All-Risks Property and Business Interruption insurance carriers will
be treated as &#147;other income&#148; if and when it is received. Following initial
discovery, the Company was granted leave of the Court to amend its complaint to
add a bad faith claim, and a claim for punitive damages.&#160; The Company has not provided for a receivable
for any of the claims in this action because of the uncertainty as to whether
and how much the Company will ultimately recover under the policies. Discovery
in the action is continuing.&#160; The Company
has also asserted that the cost of pipeline testing, replacement and repair are
subject to an equitable sharing arrangement with the pipeline owner, pursuant
to the terms of the pipeline lease agreement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company just
recently learned that a default judgment had been entered against it in May of
2006, in an action entitled <i>Runyan v. Eclipse Realty
LLC et a</i>l, (Arapahoe County District Court, Colorado, Case No.
06CV1054, filed February 2006). The Company was not aware of having ever
received a summons and was not given any notification of a motion for default
judgment.&#160; The Company is still
investigating whether there ever was proper service of process.&#160; The action involves a personal injury claim
by an individual who allegedly slipped and fell due to snowy conditions while
approaching the office building in which the Company was one of several
tenants.&#160; Eclipse Realty, the landlord of
the building, was responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the common
areas of the office building.&#160; The
Company is seeking to have the default judgment vacated, and then having the
Company dismissed as an improper party to the action.&#160; The Company also has a contractual indemnification
from Eclipse Realty, the landlord of the building, and we have demanded that
Eclipse Realty defend and indemnify the Company.&#160; We are unable to predict the outcome of our
motion to vacate the default judgment or our indemnification claim, but the
Company does not expect at this time that the matter should have a material
adverse effect on our financial position.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">The Partnership </font>received notice from one of its
customers of a potential gas measurement discrepancy and invoice errors,
claiming it is owed several hundred thousand MMBtus as a result. The
Partnership generally disputes the claims under the facts and under the terms
of the contract with the customer, but is in discussions with the customer to
evaluate and resolve all issues, and it <font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">appears
at this time that this claim should not have a material adverse impact on the
Partnership.</font></font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:36.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">With regard to the Partnership&#146;s Javelina facility,
MarkWest Javelina is a party with numerous other defendants to several lawsuits

representative of the estate of Sarina Galan Gutierrez</i> (Cause
No.&nbsp;05-2470-A, 28</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">TH</font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160;Judicial District, severed May&nbsp;18, 2005,
from the <i>Gonzales</i> case cited above);
and <i>Esmerejilda G. Valasquez, et al. v. Occidental
Chemical Corp., et al., </i><u>Case No.</u> A-060352-C, 128</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">th</font><font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&#160;Judicial District, Orange County, Texas,
